bio-w-behave.summary: Explains the same behavior in layers, from milliseconds to millions of years. It is a long book.
bio-w-behave.enRec.note: The first edition is the standard version; the paperback has the same content

bio-w-why-zebras.summary: Explains with humor how chronic stress harms the body.
bio-w-why-zebras.enRec.note: Third edition, currently the most common paperback

bio-w-in-search-memory.summary: Combines a scientist's autobiography, a history of ideas, and the neuroscience of memory.
bio-w-in-search-memory.enRec.note: An autobiography by a Nobel laureate; the Norton edition is the standard one

bio-w-descartes-error.summary: Uses cases of brain damage to show how emotion shapes rational judgment and decision-making.
bio-w-descartes-error.enRec.note: Paperback with a new preface by the author; easy to find

bio-w-determined.summary: Argues that humans have no free will and should be read alongside philosophical debates about responsibility.

bio-w-emotional-brain.summary: Explains fear and emotional memory through amygdala circuits.
bio-w-emotional-brain.enRec.note: First edition; the paperback has the same content

bio-w-how-emotions.summary: Challenges the view that there are basic emotions and argues that the brain constructs emotions.

bio-w-man-who-mistook.summary: Uses neurological case studies to show how brain damage changes a person's perception and sense of self.
bio-w-man-who-mistook.enRec.note: First edition; the paperback editions have the same content

bio-w-blueprint.summary: The author argues that DNA is the main force shaping who we are. The views are forceful and should be read alongside critics.

bio-w-who-in-charge.summary: Uses split-brain research to discuss consciousness, free will and responsibility.

bio-w-origin-of-species.summary: The original source of the theory of natural selection and the starting point for every evolutionary perspective.
bio-w-origin-of-species.enRec.note: Includes an introduction and notes, so it is easier to read

bio-w-adapted-mind.summary: A foundational collection of essays in evolutionary psychology.
bio-w-adapted-mind.enRec.note: A foundational collection of evolutionary psychology

bio-w-brain-that-changes.summary: Tells stories about neuroplasticity. Some claimed benefits are overstated, so it works best as an introduction read with a healthy dose of skepticism.
bio-w-brain-that-changes.enRec.note: First edition; the paperback has the same content

bio-w-mind-of-a-mnemonist.summary: Luria's long-term case record of a man who almost never forgot anything.
bio-w-mind-of-a-mnemonist.enRec.note: The standard English translation, with a foreword by Bruner

bio-w-the-selfish-gene.summary: Explains altruism and competition in terms of genes, and has shaped popular understanding of evolutionary thought.
bio-w-the-selfish-gene.enRec.note: Includes a new preface by the author; the current standard edition

bhv-w-dont-shoot-dog.summary: Uses everyday training examples to explain reinforcement, shaping and behavior change.

bhv-w-about-behaviorism.summary: Skinner's own clarification of common misunderstandings about behaviorism.

bhv-w-power-of-habit.summary: Uses stories to show how cues, routines and rewards form habits. The science is uneven, but it is suitable as an introduction.

bhv-w-science-human-behavior.summary: Skinner's systematic account of applying operant principles to education, government and religion.
bhv-w-science-human-behavior.enRec.note: Foundation reprint, currently the easiest version to find

bhv-w-beyond-freedom.summary: Argues that designing the behavioral environment should replace talk of "freedom and dignity," and it provoked a long debate.

bhv-w-social-learning-theory.summary: Bandura's systematic account of observational learning and the mediating role of cognition.

bhv-w-self-efficacy.summary: The most complete work on self-efficacy research.
bhv-w-self-efficacy.enRec.note: First edition; a systematic account of self-efficacy

bhv-w-conditioned-reflexes.summary: Pavlov's original work summarizing his research on conditioned reflexes.
bhv-w-conditioned-reflexes.enRec.note: Anrep's English translation; the Dover reprint is easy to find

bhv-w-atomic-habits.summary: Organizes cues, cravings, responses and rewards into practical methods for everyday habits. It is a self-help book.

bhv-w-learned-optimism.summary: Extends learned helplessness to explanatory style and training in optimism.

bhv-w-behaviorism-watson.summary: Watson's popular account of behaviorism, including the extreme environmental determinism that was later criticized.
bhv-w-behaviorism-watson.enRec.note: Reprint of the revised edition, easy to find

cog-w-thinking-fast-slow.summary: Covers heuristics, biases, intuition and deliberate thinking. Several priming studies it discusses later failed to replicate, so read it critically.
cog-w-thinking-fast-slow.enRec.note: First edition; the paperback has the same content

cog-w-seven-sins.summary: Uses seven types of memory error to explain forgetting, misremembering and suggestion.

cog-w-minds-new-science.summary: A history of how cognitive science took shape, from the cognitive revolution to artificial intelligence.

cog-w-invisible-gorilla.summary: Starts from the gorilla experiment to discuss attention, memory and the illusions of confidence.

cog-w-principles-psychology.summary: A classic foundational text of psychology. Its chapters on the stream of consciousness and habit are still readable today.

cog-w-remembering.summary: The original work on reconstructive memory, including the "War of the Ghosts" experiment.
cog-w-remembering.enRec.note: Reprint with an introduction by Kintsch

cog-w-metaphors.summary: Uses many everyday expressions to show how metaphor organizes thinking.
cog-w-metaphors.enRec.note: The standard edition, with an afterword

cog-w-embodied-mind.summary: The founding work on embodied cognition, which brings cognitive science into dialogue with Buddhist traditions of awareness.
cog-w-embodied-mind.enRec.note: Revised edition with a new introduction

cog-w-make-it-stick.summary: Turns research on retrieval practice and spaced repetition into study methods.

cog-w-surfing-uncertainty.summary: An introduction to predictive processing in philosophy and cognitive science.

cog-w-gestalt-psychology.summary: Köhler's systematic statement of Gestalt views.
cog-w-gestalt-psychology.enRec.note: The 1947 new edition, revised by the author

cog-w-geb.summary: Uses self-reference and recursion as threads to discuss mind and computation. A neighboring read for cognitive science.
cog-w-geb.enRec.note: Twentieth-anniversary edition with a new preface

dif-w-mismeasure-of-man.summary: A critique of intelligence testing and the history of race science. Some specific charges were later revised, so read it alongside the original data.
dif-w-mismeasure-of-man.enRec.note: Expanded edition, which responds to The Bell Curve

dif-w-frames-of-mind.summary: The original statement of the theory of multiple intelligences. It is best read alongside the current evidence.
dif-w-frames-of-mind.enRec.note: Tenth-anniversary edition with a new introduction

dif-w-marshmallow-test.summary: The author describes his delayed gratification research and his "if... then..." view of personality. Later replications showed that the early results were overstated.

dif-w-personality-assessment.summary: The original work that set off the person-situation debate.

dif-w-hereditary-genius.summary: The starting point of eugenics. Read it as a historical source, alongside critical literature.
dif-w-hereditary-genius.enRec.note: The original text is in the public domain and easy to find online

dif-w-intelligence-vsi.summary: A concise introduction to intelligence testing, g, and the evidence on genetic and environmental influences.

dif-w-why-we-differ.summary: Introduces modern personality psychology through the Big Five, the origins of personality, and personality dynamics.

dif-w-quiet.summary: A popular discussion of introversion and extraversion with some scientific basis. Its criticism of extravert-oriented society is advocacy.

dif-w-science-fictions.summary: Describes how fraud, bias, carelessness and hype damage scientific research, including the reproducibility crisis in psychology.
dif-w-science-fictions.enRec.note: First edition; the UK edition is the same book under the same title

dif-w-statistical-method.summary: A history of statistical thought, including Galton's work on regression and correlation. It is background reading for understanding measurement and research on differences.

dev-w-scientist-crib.summary: Uses research on infants and toddlers to show how learning, language and the mind develop.

dev-w-gardener-carpenter.summary: Turns developmental science into a reflection on parents' need for control.

dev-w-attached.summary: A popular introduction to adult attachment. The models are helpful, but people should not be permanently labeled by them.

dev-w-mind-in-society.summary: An English compilation of Vygotsky's main essays, including the discussion of the zone of proximal development.
dev-w-mind-in-society.enRec.note: An English compilation edited from Vygotsky's writings of the 1930s

dev-w-thought-language.summary: Vygotsky discusses the relationship between language and thought and critiques Piaget.
dev-w-thought-language.enRec.note: The standard English translation, with an introduction by Kozulin and a new preface

dev-w-psychology-child.summary: Piaget's concise late summary of his developmental theory.

dev-w-childhood-society.summary: The original work on the eight-stage theory, which also includes anthropology and social criticism.
dev-w-childhood-society.enRec.note: Expanded second edition, the standard version

dev-w-attachment-loss.summary: A classic statement of attachment theory. It is long and better suited to readers with some background.
dev-w-attachment-loss.enRec.note: Second edition with a new preface

dev-w-secure-base.summary: Bowlby's late lectures on the clinical application of attachment theory.
dev-w-secure-base.enRec.note: First edition; a collection of Bowlby's late lectures, which is easier to read

dev-w-ecology-human-development.summary: The original work on ecological systems theory.

dev-w-different-voice.summary: Criticizes Kohlberg and proposes the ethics of care.
dev-w-different-voice.enRec.note: New edition with a note to readers

dev-w-boy-raised-dog.summary: Uses a child case study to understand development, attachment and trauma responses.

soc-w-social-animal.summary: From conformity, prejudice and attraction to persuasion, a systematic introduction to social psychology.
soc-w-social-animal.enRec.note: A continually updated textbook-style read; the twelfth edition

soc-w-influence.summary: Uses everyday cases to explain the key mechanisms of persuasion and social influence.
soc-w-influence.enRec.note: New edition that adds a seventh principle

soc-w-righteous-mind.summary: Explains moral intuition, group identity and political division.

soc-w-nature-of-prejudice.summary: A classic study of prejudice that proposes the contact hypothesis.
soc-w-nature-of-prejudice.enRec.note: The 25th-anniversary edition, with an introduction by Clark

soc-w-happiness-hypothesis.summary: Discusses happiness, morality and human nature through ancient wisdom and modern psychology.

soc-w-the-crowd.summary: A pioneering work of crowd psychology. Read it as a text in the history of ideas, not as settled conclusions.

soc-w-obedience-authority.summary: Milgram's own account of the obedience experiments and his explanation of them.

soc-w-geography-thought.summary: Compares differences between Eastern and Western ways of thinking. Some conclusions should be treated with caution.

soc-w-mistakes-were-made.summary: Uses cognitive dissonance to explain why people find it hard to admit they were wrong.

soc-w-org-culture.summary: Schein's systematic account of organizational culture.
soc-w-org-culture.enRec.note: Fifth edition, co-written with his son Peter

soc-w-lucifer-effect.summary: Zimbardo's own account of the Stanford prison experiment, which should be read together with later criticism of it.

soc-w-culture-self.summary: The original paper on independent and interdependent views of the self.

hum-w-mans-search.summary: Introduces logotherapy and human choice through the author's life experiences.
hum-w-mans-search.enRec.note: The standard Beacon edition, with a foreword by Kushner

hum-w-on-becoming-person.summary: Explains how empathy, genuineness and unconditional positive regard support change.
hum-w-on-becoming-person.enRec.note: First edition; the Mariner paperback has the same content

hum-w-loves-executioner.summary: Uses therapy stories to explore existential themes such as death, freedom, isolation and meaning.

hum-w-flow.summary: Explains the deeply absorbing experience that occurs when ability and challenge are well matched.
